ROADMAP — DRAFT v0.3

From weekly forms to a conversation.

A three-phase plan for reducing the friction of submitting project updates — from one central form, to per-project shareable links, to a Teams bot that captures updates where the work already happens.

Phase 1 · Today

Central form + AI parse

One submission form on the dashboard. Paste a plain-English update, AI structures it into project fields with a confidence score.

✓ Shipped
Phase 2 · This quarter

Per-project share links

Every project card has a "Share update link" action. Team leads send a pre-filled URL to their contributors — no context switching, no project picker.

In progress
Phase 3 · Q3 target

Teams bot

@mention the bot in Teams with a casual update. It parses, posts to the dashboard, and DMs a review link only if confidence is low.

Designing

Phase 3 · Teams bot flow

The fewest clicks we can imagine: mention the bot, get back a ✓. Review only when uncertain.

Step 1 · User

Mentions bot in Teams

In any channel or DM, types an update as they would to a teammate.

message
Step 2 · Bot

Northline bot receives

Listens on @mention, picks up message text and author identity from Teams Graph.

payload
Step 3 · Parser

Claude structures it

Same prompt as Phase 1: match to a known project, extract status, bullets, risks, confidence.

≥ 80% confidence → auto-post
Dashboard

Logged · ✓ in Teams

Update appears under the matched project. Bot replies in thread: "Logged to Mobile App Launch · view"

< 80% confidence → DM to review
Review DM

One-tap confirm link

Bot sends user a prefilled submission link. They confirm, edit a field, or pick the right project from a list.

Happy path ≥ 80%

Clear project reference, clear status. Auto-logged.

Why this matters

Each phase compounds. The cost of submitting an update drops by an order of magnitude.

8 min
Phase 1 · Central form

One form, all projects

Leads navigate to the dashboard, find their project, fill out fields or paste a blurb.

2 min
Phase 2 · Share links

Pre-filled, locked

Direct URL per project. No picker, no context switching. Paste and submit.

15 sec
Phase 3 · Teams bot

Where the work is

Mention the bot inline. Most updates auto-log. Only ambiguous ones need a tap.

"The best status update is the one that was already being written anyway."
Phase 3 is about capturing signal that already exists in Teams — not adding another ritual.
